coverage.objective: The pleasure oral literature gives through linguistic artistry

evidence.explanation: The topic sentence says the audience and the composer enjoy various pleasures in oral literature ("Orisirisi igbadun ni onworan ati onkowe maa n je ninu litireso alohun"), but "onworan" and "onkowe" are garbled for oluworan and onikowe; line 451 begins with a stray space and lower-case "lara" so the sentence has no opening word.

Names the first pleasure, "Isowo-lo-ona ede", and lists nine devices with no definition of any: owe, akanlo-ede, "ewi tunwi", "afiwe taara", "afiwe ela loo", iforodara, asorege, "oro apara", and the abbreviation "abbl." Three of the nine ("ewi tunwi", "afiwe ela loo", "oro apara" apart) are garbled or unexplained, and the generic closing abbreviation stands where a complete list would end.

Describes the effect on the audience: the devices prevent boredom, an audience that enjoys the work will not want it to end, and will shout and clap. Both sentences are garbled: "litireso atenudanu" has no such form, "awon eniya" is misspelt, "gbadu re to bee gee" is unreadable, and "yoo maa ho yee" and "won yoo si ma patewo" do not parse. No deliverable lesson exists and the source produces no parsed row identity (Yoruba ordinal week headings; YO-FND-T1-01), so the objective is PARTIAL, not SUPPORTED.
